instruction: Select all images containing a bridge.

game.semantic_variant: Select all structures built for crossing over something.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary bridges count, and so do the bridge held up by two giant hands and the footbridge standing on insect legs: impossible, but still bridges. The fallen tree with a handrail and the stepping stones are borderline crossings, recorded without a verdict. The tunnel entrance, the outdoor staircase and the railway platform are not bridges.

correct: Bridges identified. Please cross them when you come to them.
Correct. Every bridge has been inspected.
partial: Partially correct. A bridge has been left uncrossed.
Partially correct. Some bridges escaped inspection.
incorrect: Incorrect. That bridge has been burnt.
Incorrect. The Department remains on the other side.

selection_review.reason: Version 2 of C14, replacing the photographed fallen log, which reads as a thin line at 128 px, with the re-rendered fallen tree fitted with a handrail. Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary bridges (stone packhorse arch; suspension bridge above a wooded gorge), two impossible bridges (generated road bridge held up by two giant hands; generated footbridge on insect-like legs), two borderline crossings (generated mossy fallen tree with a wooden handrail across a forest stream; photographed concrete stepping stones across a stream) and three non-members that are also built ways through or up (tunnel portal, dune staircase, railway platform). Water appears among targets and borderline cases alike; views, colours and settings vary within each role. The fallen-log photograph and the knotted bridge remain in the collection.
